articles.title: Delete submitted form data
articles.content:
API units: 25. Each accepted bulk deletion request uses 25 units.

This endpoint archives and then removes submitted data for one or more submission IDs. It removes user-entered data and action data for the selected submissions.

Endpoint and parameters

POST /api/submitted-data/{libraryId}/{serviceId}/delete
Parameter Description Required
libraryId ID of the library that owns the service. Yes
serviceId ID of the service containing the submissions. Yes

Request

Send the API key in the Authorization header and JSON in the request body.

Header Value
Authorization GovformsApiKey {keyId}:{keySecret}
Content-Type application/json 
{
  "submissionIds": [
    "1234-ABCD-ABCD",
    "5678-EFGH-EFGH"
  ]
}

submissionIds must be a non-empty array. A request can contain at most 1000 IDs.

Successful response

{
  "requestedCount": 2,
  "deletedCount": 1,
  "deletedSubmissionIds": ["1234-ABCD-ABCD"],
  "notFoundSubmissionIds": ["5678-EFGH-EFGH"]
}
Field Meaning
requestedCount Number of non-empty submission IDs accepted from the request.
deletedCount Number of submitted-data records deleted.
deletedSubmissionIds IDs found and deleted.
notFoundSubmissionIds IDs not found for this library and service.

Errors

Status Reason
400 Missing parameters, or submissionIds is missing, empty or not an array.
403 The key is invalid, lacks permission for this endpoint, or the request IP is not allowed.
404 The service was not found.
413 More than 1000 submission IDs were supplied.
500 Server error.

articles.title: Response Hub API
articles.content:
API units: Response Hub pages are capped at 100 records and use 5 units. Roster and export data operations use 25 units.

API units by operation

OperationUnits
List or get services, collections, cohorts, assignments, responses, reviews, communications or audit records5
Create, update, transition, assign, cancel or review5
Poll an export or fetch its manifest1
Start an export or download each export part25
Stage or apply a roster25

Only successful calls and accepted asynchronous jobs consume monthly units.

Use the Response Hub API to automate recurring data collections, manage respondent assignments and work with submitted responses and reviews.

The API is hosted by Govforms Builder. It securely routes each request to the collection environment specified in the path.

Before you start

Create an API key from Library settings → Govforms API keys. Grant only the permissions the integration needs:

  • apiResponseHubRead — read services, collections, respondent organisations and contacts, assignments, submitted answer versions, reviews, communications and audit events.
  • apiResponseHubWrite — create and update services and collections; manage lifecycle, cohorts, assignments, rosters and reviews. Write permission also permits reads.
  • apiFormWrite — additionally required when creating a collection because Govforms creates its managed form from a saved form version.
  • apiFormDeploy — additionally required to prepare the latest collection form for QA, Staging or Production.

Form-design permissions and Response Hub data permissions are independent. A key can work with forms without seeing live Response Hub data, or work with Response Hub without seeing unrelated form designs.

Base URL and authentication

All paths use the Builder base URL:

https://govforms.uk/builder/libraries/{libraryId}/api/response-hub

Send Authorization: GovformsApiKey KEY_ID:SECRET_VALUE and Content-Type: application/json. HMAC authentication is recommended. An optional X-On-Behalf-Of header can identify the responsible user or integration in audit records.

Every request is restricted to the library in the path. Environments are qa, staging where enabled, and production. List operations accept page and pageSize, capped at 100; relevant operations also accept search, sort and assignment filters.

Data collection services

  • GET /services — list data collection services.
  • POST /services — create a data collection service.
  • GET /services/{serviceId} — get service defaults and message templates.
  • PATCH /services/{serviceId} — update the service name, defaults and templates used by future collections.

Collections and form application

  • GET /services/{serviceId}/collections/{environment} — list collections.
  • POST /services/{serviceId}/collections — create a collection and managed form from a saved source form version.
  • GET /services/{serviceId}/collections/{environment}/{collectionId} — get one collection.
  • PATCH /services/{serviceId}/collections/{environment}/{collectionId} — update a draft collection.
  • POST /services/{serviceId}/collections/{environment}/{collectionId}/transition/{action} — open, close or reopen a collection. Reopening requires a reason.
  • POST /services/{serviceId}/collections/{environment}/{collectionId}/apply-form — apply the latest saved collection form.
  • GET /services/{serviceId}/collections/{environment}/{collectionId}/form-revisions — list applied revision metadata. Form definitions are intentionally omitted.

Applying a form in QA, Staging or Production prepares a deployment and returns an approvalUrl. An authorised person must open that link to confirm the change. This keeps the existing human deployment boundary.

Cohorts, assignments and rosters

  • GET .../{collectionId}/cohorts — list cohorts.
  • POST .../{collectionId}/cohorts — create a cohort with optional policy overrides.
  • PATCH .../{collectionId}/cohorts/{cohortId} — update a non-default cohort before opening.
  • GET .../{collectionId}/assignments — list assignments with organisation, contact, response and review context.
  • POST .../{collectionId}/assignments — create or update an assignment using a stable external organisation ID.
  • POST .../{collectionId}/assignments/{assignmentId}/cancel — cancel an assignment while preserving response history.
  • POST .../{collectionId}/roster — stage and validate a base64-encoded CSV roster.
  • POST .../{collectionId}/roster/{rosterJobId}/apply — apply a staged roster in merge or replace mode.

Roster staging does not change respondents. It returns a preview of creates, updates, unchanged assignments and omissions so the result can be checked before applying it.

Responses, reviews, communications and audit

  • GET .../{collectionId}/responses/{responseId} — get a response, immutable submitted answer versions, active review and issues.
  • GET .../{collectionId}/reviews — list available and claimed review work.
  • GET .../{collectionId}/reviews/{workItemId} — get one review and its submitted answer version.
  • POST .../{collectionId}/reviews/{workItemId}/{action} — claim, accept, return, release, reassign or add an issue.
  • GET .../{collectionId}/communications — list queued, sent, failed and cancelled respondent messages.
  • GET .../{collectionId}/audit — list append-only collection audit events.

Review commands accept an optional commandId for safe retry. Returning, releasing and reassigning require a reason. Submitted versions are immutable: the API returns the answer snapshot associated with the selected version, not a later form design.

Example

Create a data collection service:

POST /builder/libraries/demo-library/api/response-hub/services
Authorization: GovformsApiKey KEY_ID:SECRET_VALUE
Content-Type: application/json

{
 "collectionServiceId": "annual-returns",
 "name": "Annual returns",
 "defaults": {
   "retentionDays": 2555
 }
}

Errors and safe retries

Errors return JSON with an error.message. Typical statuses are 400 for invalid input, 403 for an invalid key or missing permission, 404 when a scoped record is not found, and 409 for an invalid lifecycle transition.

Read operations are safe to retry. Reuse a review command's commandId. Roster import is deliberately staged and applied in two calls. Collection IDs, response versions and audit history are never replaced by update requests.

‍

articles.title: Govforms MCP capabilities
articles.content:
MCP API units: Each tools/call is charged by the operation it runs. Initialization, tool discovery, resources and prompts do not use monthly units.

MCP API units

Tool operationUnits
Darcy calls; status, summary, permission and export polling1
Lists, searches, full service reads, Response Hub pages up to 100 records and ordinary changes5
Full-definition saves, pages over 100 records, export start/download and roster stage/apply25

Every tools/call in a JSON-RPC batch is admitted and charged separately. Successful results include _meta.govformsApiUsage. Quota errors include the equivalent usage fields in JSON-RPC error.data. Operations affecting more than one account charge once per affected account and group authorised libraries that share each balance.

Govforms MCP lets an AI agent inspect and manage Govforms through structured, permission-aware tools. It can work with form designs and with Response Hub data while keeping those two areas separate.

What an agent can do

Depending on the access granted, an agent can:

  • find libraries, services and reusable patterns;
  • inspect form structure, settings, conditions, actions and deployment status;
  • create and update forms through structured Govforms tools;
  • prepare deployments and undeployments;
  • list Response Hub data collection services and collections;
  • manage collection lifecycle, cohorts, respondent assignments and roster imports;
  • read immutable submitted response versions and review issues;
  • claim, return, accept, release, reassign or complete Response Hub reviews;
  • inspect respondent communications and the collection audit trail.

Govforms also exposes guidance resources that help an agent understand the platform model and choose a safe tool before making changes.

You choose the access

Interactive MCP uses your Govforms sign-in. When connecting an MCP client, every library has two independent access choices:

Form designs

  • No access — the agent cannot see forms in that library.
  • Read-only — the agent can inspect forms and deployment status.
  • Full access — the agent may update forms or prepare deployments where the signed-in person's Govforms role also allows it.

Response Hub data

  • No access — the agent cannot see collections, respondents or submissions.
  • Read-only — the agent can inspect collections, submitted responses, reviews, communications and audit history.
  • Full access — the agent may manage collections, assignments, rosters and reviews where the signed-in person's Govforms role also allows it.

Nothing is selected by default. Govforms checks both the connection grant and the person's current library role on every call. If that role changes or is removed, the connection immediately follows the new access.

This makes it possible to let an agent improve a form without exposing live respondent data, let an operational agent triage submissions without access to unrelated form designs, or give an audit agent read-only access to both areas.

Ways to connect

Interactive OAuth is recommended for people using an agent directly. Connect the MCP client to:

https://govforms.uk/builder/mcp

The person signs in to Govforms, selects libraries, then separately chooses form-design and Response Hub access for each one.

API-key MCP is designed for controlled server-side integrations. Its endpoint is:

https://govforms.uk/builder/libraries/{libraryId}/mcp

API key permissions separately control form reads, form writes, deployments, Response Hub reads and Response Hub writes. The tool catalogue only includes operations allowed by that key.

Response Hub tools

Read tools list services, collections, cohorts, assignments, immutable submitted response versions, reviews, communications, audit events and applied form-revision metadata.

Write tools create or update services and collections, change collection lifecycle, apply saved forms, manage cohorts and assignments, stage and apply rosters, and perform review actions.

Creating a collection also requires form-write access. Applying a collection form also requires deployment access. These extra checks prevent Response Hub access from becoming an indirect route to unrelated form-design changes.

Safety boundaries

  • Every operation is restricted to the selected library.
  • Response Hub records are also restricted to one data collection service, collection and environment.
  • Read-only grants cannot invoke mutating tools.
  • Form-design access does not imply Response Hub access, or the reverse.
  • The signed-in person's current Govforms role remains the upper limit for interactive MCP.
  • Applying a collection form to QA, Staging or Production returns a human approval step.
  • Submitted Response Hub versions and audit records remain immutable.
  • Tools identify read-only, destructive and externally visible operations for MCP clients.

Treat agent access as sensitive. Start with read-only access, select only the libraries and areas needed, inspect planned changes, and grant full access only to workflows that are understood and supervised.

‍

articles.title: Write Liquid templates
articles.content:
Liquid lets a Govforms service read journey data and turn it into the value required by a setting. That value is not always page content: the same language can decide a condition, build an API payload, calculate a field value, create Markdown or HTML, or supply a short label.

Start with the output contract: identify whether the setting expects a Boolean, JSON, XML, Markdown, HTML, plain text or another value. Then write and test the smallest template that produces exactly that shape.

Where Liquid is used

UseExpected resultTypical example
Condition templatetrue or falseDecide whether a route or action should run.
API action URL, headers or bodyURL text, JSON, XML or another API-specific payloadSend selected answers and action results to another service.
Markdown or HTML contentReadable contentPersonalise information, confirmation or review content.
Assign action or pre-populated valueA string, number, object, array or field-specific valueStore a calculation or prepare repeated rows.
Labels, button text and other short settingsPlain textInclude a name or status in a concise label.

Liquid syntax essentials

Use output tags to print a value, and tag blocks to control logic:

{{ first_name }}
{% if applicant_age >= 18 %}
  Adult
{% else %}
  Under 18
{% endif %}
  • Do not put parentheses around Liquid conditions. Write {% if age >= 18 %}, not {% if (age >= 18) %}.
  • Liquid does not support JavaScript-style array literals. Use split, parse_json, or the Govforms array filter.
  • Add non-output notes with {% comment %}...{% endcomment %}.
  • Use stable IDs for fields, actions and conditions. Visible labels can change without changing those IDs.

Understand the Liquid context

Govforms makes the current journey context available to Liquid. Field values sit at the root, while service metadata and runtime results are grouped under named objects.

ContextWhat it containsExample
Field IDs at the rootThe current value of each field.{{ first_name }}
formJourney and service metadata, the signed-in user where available, URL query parameters, page position and repeating-row context.{{ form.submissionId }}
conditionsThe current true or false result of each condition, keyed by Condition ID.{% if conditions.is_eligible %}
actionsResults from actions that have already run, keyed by Action ID.{{ actions.find_account.response }}
cartsKeyed collections that persist across pages in the journey.{{ carts.appointments[selected_id] }}
nowThe current date and time.{{ now | format_date: "dd MMMM yyyy" }}

Homepage templates can also receive journey collections such as open, completed, workflow, closed and cancelled journeys. Each entry uses the same context shape, so read only the fields and metadata required by the homepage component.

Read field values

Most fields are available directly by Field ID:

{{ first_name }}
{{ contact_method }}
{{ selected_topics | join: ", " }}

A radio or select field contains the selected item ID. A checkbox field contains an array of selected item IDs. Use lookup_item_label when a person-facing label is needed.

Structured fields expose properties:

{{ appointment_date.day }}/{{ appointment_date.month }}/{{ appointment_date.year }}
{{ appointment_time.hour }}:{{ appointment_time.minute }}
{{ home_address.line1 }}, {{ home_address.postcode }}
{{ chosen_location.lat }}, {{ chosen_location.lng }}

Date fields use day, month and year; time fields use hour and minute. Address fields can include line1 to line5, postcode and country. Map-select fields can include lat, lng, bng, nearPlace and nearFullDescription.

Use repeating-group values

Groups do not have a user-entered Liquid ID. The outer group’s identifier is generated and is not referenced by conditions, actions or templates. Give each field inside the group a stable Field ID and use those IDs directly.

Every inner field becomes an array with one value per repetition. Use one field as the loop and the same index to read its neighbours:

{% for name in attendee_name %}
- {{ attendee_name[forloop.index0] }} — {{ attendee_email[forloop.index0] }}
{% endfor %}

When a template is evaluated inside a row, currentRepeat0 and this identify the zero-based row. For pre-population, configure each inner field—not the group—and return a JSON array with one value per row:

{% assign names = actions.get_staff.response.data | map: "staffName" %}
{{ names | json }}

Read form metadata and query parameters

Common metadata includes form.submissionId, form.libraryId, form.serviceId, form.title, form.environment, status values and current-user information where authentication provides it.

Read a URL query parameter through form.query:

{{ form.query.caseId }}

Query parameters are rebuilt from the current URL on each page. They do not automatically survive a redirect. Pass required parameters explicitly in the Redirect action or with a navigation filter such as page_link.

Read condition results

Conditions are keyed by Condition ID and resolve to true or false. They can be reused without reproducing the condition logic:

{% if conditions.can_submit %}
  Ready to submit
{% else %}
  Check the missing information
{% endif %}

A condition template itself should produce a clear Boolean result:

{% if applicant_age >= 18 and country_code == "GB" %}true{% else %}false{% endif %}

Read action results

Only actions that have already run are available. Every action result can include responseCode, executionTime and error. Action-specific values depend on the action type.

Action resultTypical access
API response{{ actions.get_record.response.data.items }}
Feed lookup rows{{ actions.find_rows.response }} or {{ actions.find_rows.results }}
Assigned value{{ actions.calculate_total.value }}
Generated PDF{{ actions.create_pdf.base64 }}
Authorization result{{ actions.check_access.hasAccess }}
Uploaded file result{{ actions.upload_document.fileUrl }}

Test the failure path as well as the successful response. Check responseCode or error before assuming nested response properties exist.

Work with carts

A cart stores items by Cart ID and Item ID and persists across pages. Values can be strings, numbers, objects or arrays.

{{ carts.appointments }}
{{ carts.appointments.monday_morning }}
{{ carts.appointments.monday_morning.location }}
{{ carts.appointments[form.query.itemId].location }}

Populate carts with “Add or update items in a cart” actions and remove entries with the corresponding remove action. Use bracket notation when the item ID comes from a field or query parameter.

Produce the right output type

Boolean

Return true or false for condition and authorization checks. Keep the rule readable and test missing values.

JSON

Use json to serialize an object or array. Use to_json_string when a string value needs its own surrounding JSON quotes, or jsonstr when it is already inside quotes:

{
  "submissionId": {{ form.submissionId | to_json_string }},
  "name": {{ full_name | to_json_string }},
  "topics": {{ selected_topics | json }},
  "note": "{{ case_note | jsonstr }}"
}

Use parse_json to turn JSON text into an object or array. There is no Govforms to_json filter; use json, jsonstr or to_json_string according to the required shape.

XML

Escape dynamic text for XML rather than HTML:

<request><name>{{ full_name | xml_escape }}</name></request>

Markdown or HTML

Markdown is usually the clearest choice for headings, lists and links in content settings. When a setting accepts HTML, escape untrusted text before inserting it into markup:

## Application for {{ full_name }}

- Reference: {{ form.submissionId }}

<strong>{{ full_name | escape }}</strong>

Plain text and typed values

Labels normally expect short plain text. Assign actions and pre-populated values may expect a number, object or array instead. Confirm the target field’s value shape before returning structured data.

Create arrays and objects

Create an array from text with split, an empty array with parse_json, or an array from variables with the Govforms array filter:

{% assign routes = "email,phone,post" | split: "," %}
{% assign empty_items = "[]" | parse_json %}
{% assign selected = first_item | array: second_item, third_item %}

Use set to add or replace an object property. It is different from the built-in push filter, which appends an item to an array.

Test before publishing

  • Confirm that the setting supports Liquid and identify its exact output type.
  • Test normal, blank, missing, repeated, very long and unexpected values.
  • Test every branch of condition logic and both success and failure action results.
  • Validate JSON or XML payloads with representative quotes, line breaks and non-ASCII characters.
  • Check that IDs are stable and refer to inner fields rather than a repeating group.
  • Test revisiting a page, resuming a draft and running an action more than once.
  • Test in User view and the appropriate QA environment before deployment.

Filter reference

  • Arrays and collections filters
  • Text and formatting filters
  • Data, objects and encoding filters
  • Dates, times and number filters
  • Links and navigation filters
  • Forms, fields and service filters

articles.title: Arrays and collections
articles.content:
Use these filters to create, combine, search, group and reshape collections. In repeating groups, work with the arrays stored under each inner field ID; the group itself is not a Liquid value.

Standard Liquid filters

These filters are provided as standard by the Liquid language. They are available anywhere Govforms accepts a Liquid template.

FilterWhat it doesExample
array_to_sentence_string(connector)Joins array items as a sentence
Separates items with commas and uses the connector before the final item.		{{ names | array_to_sentence_string: "and" }} → Alex, Sam, and Jo
compact()Removes nil values from array
Filters out null and undefined values.		{{ array | compact }} → removes nil values
concat(array)Concatenates arrays
Combines input array with another array.		{{ arr1 | concat: arr2 }} → combined array
find(property, expected)Finds the first matching array item
Returns the first object whose property equals the expected value. If expected is omitted, the property must be truthy.		{{ users | find: "name", "Sam" | json }}
find_exp(item_name, expression)Finds the first array item matching an expression
Evaluates a Liquid expression for each item and returns the first match.		{{ users | find_exp: "user", "user.age >= 18" | json }}
find_index(property, expected)Finds the index of the first matching array item
Returns the zero-based index of the first object whose property matches.		{{ users | find_index: "name", "Sam" }}
find_index_exp(item_name, expression)Finds the index of the first item matching an expression
Evaluates a Liquid expression for each item and returns the first matching zero-based index.		{{ users | find_index_exp: "user", "user.age >= 18" }}
first()Gets first element of array
Returns first item in array or first character of string.		{{ "hello" | first }} → h
group_by(property)Groups array items by a property
Returns groups with name and items properties for each distinct property value.		{{ users | group_by: "team" | json }}
group_by_exp(item_name, expression)Groups array items using an expression
Evaluates a Liquid expression for each item and groups items by the result.		{{ users | group_by_exp: "user", "user.age >= 18" | json }}
has(property, expected)Checks whether an array contains a matching item
Returns true when an object property matches the expected value.		{{ users | has: "name", "Sam" }} → true
has_exp(item_name, expression)Checks whether any array item matches an expression
Returns true when the Liquid expression is true for at least one item.		{{ users | has_exp: "user", "user.age >= 18" }} → true
join(separator)Joins array elements with separator
Concatenates array items with specified separator.		{{ "a,b,c" | split: "," | join: " - " }} → a - b - c
last()Gets last element of array
Returns last item in array or last character of string.		{{ "hello" | last }} → o
map(property)Extracts property from array of objects
Creates array of property values from object array.		{{ users | map: "name" }} → array of name values
pop()Removes the last array item
Returns a copy of the array without its final item.		{{ values | pop | json }}
push(item)Adds an item to the end of an array
Returns a copy of the array with the supplied item appended.		{{ values | push: new_value | json }}
reject(property, expected)Rejects matching array items
Returns objects whose property does not equal the expected value. If expected is omitted, rejects truthy properties.		{{ users | reject: "inactive", true | json }}
reject_exp(item_name, expression)Rejects array items matching an expression
Returns items for which the Liquid expression evaluates to false.		{{ users | reject_exp: "user", "user.inactive" | json }}
reverse()Reverses array or string
Returns array/string with elements in reverse order.		{{ "hello" | reverse }} → olleh
sample(count)Selects random array items or characters
Returns one random item by default, or an array containing the requested number of random items.		{{ values | sample }}
shift()Removes the first array item
Returns a copy of the array without its first item.		{{ values | shift | json }}
size()Returns size of array or string
Gets length/count of elements.		{{ "hello" | size }} → 5
slice(start, length)Extracts substring or subarray
Returns portion starting at index for specified length.		{{ "hello" | slice: 1, 3 }} → ell
sort(property)Sorts array
Sorts array elements, optionally by property name.		{{ "b,a,c" | split: "," | sort | join: "," }} → a,b,c
sort_natural(property)Sorts array using natural ordering
Sorts with natural number ordering (10 after 2).		{{ "item10,item2,item1" | split: "," | sort_natural | join: "," }} → item1,item2,item10
sum(property)Adds array values
Returns the total of numeric array values, optionally reading a property from each object.		{{ order_items | sum: "price" }}
uniq()Removes duplicate values from array
Returns array with unique elements only.		{{ [1,2,2,3] | uniq }} → [1,2,3]
unshift(item)Adds an item to the start of an array
Returns a copy of the array with the supplied item prepended.		{{ values | unshift: new_value | json }}
where(property, expected)Selects matching array items
Returns objects whose property equals the expected value. If expected is omitted, the property must be truthy.		{{ users | where: "active", true | json }}
where_exp(item_name, expression)Selects array items matching an expression
Returns items for which the Liquid expression evaluates to true.		{{ users | where_exp: "user", "user.age >= 18" | json }}

Govforms filters

These filters are added by Govforms for service-building and data-handling tasks.

FilterWhat it doesExample
array(...items)Creates array from arguments
Constructs array from provided values.		{{ "item1" | array: "item2", "item3" }}
clone(object)Creates deep copy of object
Returns structurally cloned copy of the object.		{{ original_object | clone }}
delete(object, key)Removes property from object
Deletes the specified key from the object.		{{ my_object | delete: "unwanted_key" }}
equals_or_includes(value, item)Checks equality or array inclusion
Returns true if value equals item, or if value is array containing item.		{{ field_value | equals_or_includes: "target" }}
includes_item(array, item)Checks if array contains specific item
Returns true if the item is found in the array.		{{ my_array | includes_item: "search_value" }}
is_array(value)Checks if value is an array
Returns true if value is an array object.		{{ my_value | is_array }}
num_items(object)Returns number of properties in object
Counts the number of keys in an object.		{{ my_object | num_items }}
object_keys(object)Returns array of object property names
Gets all enumerable property names from the object.		{{ my_object | object_keys }}
object_values(object)Returns array of object property values
Gets all enumerable property values from the object.		{{ my_object | object_values }}
remove_empty_arrays(object)Removes empty arrays from objects recursively
Cleans objects by removing properties whose value is an empty array.		{{ form_data | remove_empty_arrays }}
remove_empty_objects(object)Removes empty objects from objects recursively
Cleans objects by removing properties whose value is an object with no properties.		{{ form_data | remove_empty_objects }}
remove_empty_properties(object)Removes empty properties from objects recursively
Cleans objects by removing null, undefined, empty strings, and empty arrays/objects.		{{ my_object | remove_empty_properties }}
remove_internal_properties(object)Removes internal properties from objects recursively
Cleans objects by removing properties whose name starts with an underscore.		{{ form_data | remove_internal_properties }}
remove_null_properties(object)Removes null properties from objects recursively
Cleans objects by removing properties whose value is null.		{{ form_data | remove_null_properties }}
remove_properties_from_object(object, ...keys)Removes specific properties by key from objects recursively
Removes all properties matching the specified keys throughout the object tree.		{{ my_object | remove_properties_from_object: "password", "token" }}
set(object, key, value)Sets property on object
Assigns value to the specified key on the object.		{{ my_object | set: "new_key", "new_value" }}
with_attribute(html_string, attribute_name, attribute_value)Adds HTML attribute to element
Takes an HTML element string and adds the specified attribute with value. Useful for adding ARIA attributes, data attributes, or other HTML attributes to dynamically generated elements. The attribute value is automatically escaped to prevent XSS.		{{ '<button type="button">Click</button>' | with_attribute: "aria-label", "Submit form" }}

Related guidance

  • Write Liquid templates
  • Use Markdown and HTML

articles.title: Text and formatting
articles.content:
Use these filters to prepare human-readable text and to escape values for HTML or XML. Choose the escaping filter for the output type: HTML, XML, JSON and URL output have different rules.

Standard Liquid filters

These filters are provided as standard by the Liquid language. They are available anywhere Govforms accepts a Liquid template.

FilterWhat it doesExample
append(string)Appends string to input
Concatenates string to the end of input.		{{ "Hello" | append: " World" }} → Hello World
capitalize()Capitalizes first letter of string
Makes first character uppercase, rest lowercase.		{{ "hello world" | capitalize }} → Hello world
downcase()Converts string to lowercase
Makes all characters lowercase.		{{ "HELLO" | downcase }} → hello
escape()HTML escapes string
Escapes HTML special characters.		{{ "<script>" | escape }} → <script>
escape_once()HTML escapes string only if not already escaped
Prevents double-escaping of HTML.		{{ "<div>" | escape_once }} → <div>
lstrip()Removes whitespace from left side
Trims whitespace from beginning of string.		{{ " hello" | lstrip }} → hello
newline_to_br()Converts newlines to HTML breaks
Replaces with <br> tags.		{{ "line1 line2" | newline_to_br }} → line1<br /> line2
normalize_whitespace()Normalizes whitespace
Replaces each run of whitespace characters with one space.		{{ "Hello World" | normalize_whitespace }} → Hello World
number_of_words(mode)Counts words in text
Counts whitespace-separated words. Use "cjk" or "auto" to count CJK characters appropriately.		{{ "one two three" | number_of_words }} → 3
prepend(string)Prepends string to input
Concatenates string to beginning of input.		{{ "World" | prepend: "Hello " }} → Hello World
remove(substring)Removes all occurrences of substring
Removes every instance of substring from input.		{{ "Hello World" | remove: "l" }} → Heo Word
remove_first(substring)Removes first occurrence of substring
Removes only the first instance of substring.		{{ "Hello World" | remove_first: "l" }} → Helo World
remove_last(substring)Removes the last occurrence of a substring
Removes only the final instance of the supplied substring.		{{ "Hello Hello" | remove_last: "Hello" }} → Hello
replace(search, replacement)Replaces all occurrences of search with replacement
Substitutes every instance of search string.		{{ "Hello World" | replace: "World", "Universe" }} → Hello Universe
replace_first(search, replacement)Replaces first occurrence of search with replacement
Substitutes only the first instance of search string.		{{ "Hello Hello" | replace_first: "Hello", "Hi" }} → Hi Hello
replace_last(search, replacement)Replaces the last occurrence of text
Substitutes only the final instance of the search string.		{{ "Hello Hello" | replace_last: "Hello", "World" }} → Hello World
rstrip()Removes whitespace from right side
Trims whitespace from end of string.		{{ "hello " | rstrip }} → hello
split(separator)Splits string into array
Divides string at separator characters.		{{ "a,b,c" | split: "," }} → ["a", "b", "c"]
strip()Removes whitespace from both sides
Trims whitespace from beginning and end.		{{ " hello " | strip }} → hello
strip_html()Removes HTML tags from string
Strips all HTML markup, leaving text content.		{{ "<p>Hello</p>" | strip_html }} → Hello
strip_newlines()Removes newline characters
Removes and characters from string.		{{ "line1 line2" | strip_newlines }} → line1line2
truncate(length, ellipsis)Truncates string to maximum length
Cuts string at length, optionally adding ellipsis.		{{ "Hello World" | truncate: 8, "..." }} → Hello...
truncatewords(word_count, ellipsis)Truncates to maximum word count
Cuts string after specified number of words.		{{ "Hello World Test" | truncatewords: 2 }} → Hello World...
upcase()Converts string to uppercase
Makes all characters uppercase.		{{ "hello" | upcase }} → HELLO
xml_escape()Escapes text for XML
Replaces XML special characters with safe entity references.		{{ "<item>A & B</item>" | xml_escape }}

Govforms filters

These filters are added by Govforms for service-building and data-handling tasks.

FilterWhat it doesExample
decompress_text(base64_brotli_string)Decompresses Brotli-compressed text stored as base64
Decodes a base64 string containing Brotli-compressed UTF-8 text, such as HTML generated by the Generate HTML action.		{{ actions.myHtmlAction.compressedHtml | decompress_text }}
field_to_text(field_value, field_id, field_defs, part_id)Converts field value to display text
Formats field value according to field type for display.		{{ my_field_value | field_to_text: "field1", form.fieldDefs }}
form_to_text(form, newlines)Converts form data to formatted text
Creates human-readable text summary of form data.		{{ form | form_to_text: 2 }}
lookup_item_id(item_text, field_id)Gets the ID for a choice item by display text
Reverse lookup to find choice ID from display text.		{{ "Option A" | lookup_item_id: "my_field" }}
lookup_item_label(item_id, field_id)Gets the display text for a choice item by ID
Looks up choice text from field definition using the choice ID.		{{ "choice1" | lookup_item_label: "my_field" }}
remove_empty_strings(object)Removes empty strings from objects recursively
Cleans objects and arrays by removing properties whose value is an empty string.		{{ form_data | remove_empty_strings }}

Related guidance

  • Use Markdown and HTML

articles.title: Data, objects and encoding
articles.content:
Use these filters to serialize and parse data, inspect values, read variables and prepare safe payloads. Treat action responses and incoming data as untrusted, and encode for the destination rather than applying HTML escaping by habit.

Base64 compatibility: LiquidJS and Govforms both expose base64_encode and base64_decode. Govforms supplies compatible implementations in the running service, so the same Liquid syntax is used.

Standard Liquid filters

These filters are provided as standard by the Liquid language. They are available anywhere Govforms accepts a Liquid template.

FilterWhat it doesExample
base64_decode()Decodes base64 text
Converts a base64-encoded string back to UTF-8 text.		{{ "SGVsbG8=" | base64_decode }} → Hello
base64_encode()Encodes text as base64
Converts text or binary data to a base64-encoded string.		{{ "Hello" | base64_encode }} → SGVsbG8=
default(fallback)Provides fallback for empty values
Returns fallback if input is null, undefined, or empty string.		{{ empty_var | default: "N/A" }} → N/A
hmac_sha256(secret_key)Creates an HMAC-SHA256 signature
Signs the input using the supplied secret key and returns a hexadecimal digest.		{{ message | hmac_sha256: secret_key }}
inspect(spaces)Converts a value to readable JSON
Serializes a value as JSON, with optional indentation for inspection.		{{ form | inspect: 2 }}
json()Converts value to JSON string
Serializes value as JSON.		{{ my_object | json }} → {"key":"value"}
jsonify(spaces)Converts a value to JSON
Serializes a value as JSON, with optional indentation.		{{ form | jsonify }}
raw()Outputs a value without escaping
Marks the value as raw output. Only use this with content that is safe to render.		{{ trusted_html | raw }}
sha256()Creates a SHA-256 digest
Hashes the input and returns its hexadecimal SHA-256 digest.		{{ message | sha256 }}
to_integer()Converts a value to an integer
Parses the input as a base-10 whole number.		{{ "42" | to_integer }} → 42

Govforms filters

These filters are added by Govforms for service-building and data-handling tasks.

FilterWhat it doesExample
base64_decode(string)Decodes base64 string
Converts base64 encoded string back to UTF-8 text.		{{ "aGVsbG8=" | base64_decode }} → hello
base64_encode(string)Encodes string as base64
Converts string to base64 encoding using Buffer.		{{ "hello" | base64_encode }} → aGVsbG8=
form_to_json(form)Converts form data to JSON object
Extracts all field values into clean JSON structure.		{{ form | form_to_json }}
get_var(variable_name)Gets variable value by name from context
Dynamically retrieves a variable value using its name as a string.		{{ "ke1individStratObj_3" | get_var }}
jsonstr(string)Escapes string for JSON without outer quotes
Like to_json_string but removes the surrounding quotes.		{{ "hello world" | jsonstr }} → hello\nworld
odata_string_escape(string)Escapes string for OData queries
Escapes single quotes for use in OData query strings.		{{ "O'Reilly" | odata_string_escape }} → O''Reilly
parse_json(json_string)Parses JSON string into object
Converts JSON string back into JavaScript object.		{{ '{"key": "value"}' | parse_json }}
remove_data_url_properties(object)Removes properties containing data URLs from objects
Recursively removes properties that contain base64 data URLs.		{{ form_data | remove_data_url_properties }}
to_json_string(value)Converts value to JSON string format
Properly escapes value for use in JSON, including quotes.		{{ my_value | to_json_string }}
uuid()Generates unique identifier
Creates a new UUID string.		{{ "" | uuid }} → generates random UUID
xpath(xml_string, xpath_expression, single)Extracts data from XML using XPath expressions
Parses XML and applies XPath query. Set single to "single" for single result.		{{ xml_data | xpath: "//item/@id" }}

Related guidance

  • Write Liquid templates
  • Use Markdown and HTML

articles.title: Dates, times and numbers
articles.content:
Use these filters for arithmetic, dates, time zones and numeric presentation. Test boundary cases around midnight, daylight-saving changes, month ends, blanks and values supplied as text.

Standard Liquid filters

These filters are provided as standard by the Liquid language. They are available anywhere Govforms accepts a Liquid template.

FilterWhat it doesExample
abs(number)Returns absolute value of number
Converts negative numbers to positive.		{{ -5 | abs }} → 5
at_least(minimum)Ensures value is at least minimum
Returns input if >= minimum, otherwise returns minimum.		{{ 3 | at_least: 5 }} → 5
at_most(maximum)Ensures value is at most maximum
Returns input if <= maximum, otherwise returns maximum.		{{ 10 | at_most: 5 }} → 5
ceil()Rounds number up to nearest integer
Returns smallest integer >= input.		{{ 4.2 | ceil }} → 5
date(format)Formats date string
Formats date using strftime format codes.		{{ "now" | date: "%Y-%m-%d" }} → 2025-03-15
date_to_long_string(type, style)Formats a date with the full month name
Returns a date such as 25 December 2026. Use "ordinal" and optionally "US" for an ordinal date.		{{ "2026-12-25" | date_to_long_string }} → 25 December 2026
date_to_rfc822()Formats a date as RFC 822
Returns a date and time suitable for feeds and email date headers.		{{ "2026-07-23T12:30:00Z" | date_to_rfc822 }}
date_to_string(type, style)Formats a date with an abbreviated month
Returns a date such as 25 Dec 2026. Use "ordinal" and optionally "US" for an ordinal date.		{{ "2026-12-25" | date_to_string }} → 25 Dec 2026
date_to_xmlschema()Formats a date as an XML Schema timestamp
Returns an ISO-style date and time including its time zone offset.		{{ "2026-07-23T12:30:00Z" | date_to_xmlschema }}
divided_by(divisor)Divides number by divisor
Performs division operation.		{{ 10 | divided_by: 3 }} → 3.3333333333333335
floor()Rounds number down to nearest integer
Returns largest integer <= input.		{{ 4.8 | floor }} → 4
minus(subtrahend)Subtracts number from input
Performs subtraction operation.		{{ 10 | minus: 3 }} → 7
modulo(divisor)Returns remainder after division
Performs modulo operation.		{{ 10 | modulo: 3 }} → 1
plus(addend)Adds number to input
Performs addition operation.		{{ 5 | plus: 3 }} → 8
round(decimal_places)Rounds number to specified decimal places
Rounds to nearest value with specified precision.		{{ 3.14159 | round: 2 }} → 3.14
times(multiplier)Multiplies number by multiplier
Performs multiplication operation.		{{ 3 | times: 4 }} → 12

Govforms filters

These filters are added by Govforms for service-building and data-handling tasks.

FilterWhat it doesExample
as_number(string)Converts string to number, removing currency symbols
Parses numeric value from string, removing £, $, €, and commas.		{{ "£1,234.56" | as_number }} → 1234.56
date_to_gfdate(date, time_zone)Converts JavaScript Date to Govforms date object
Transforms Date to {day, month, year} object format. Optionally extracts the date in the supplied IANA time zone.		{{ my_date | date_to_gfdate: "Europe/London" }}
day_end(date, offset, time_zone)Gets end of day (23:59:59)
Returns date at end of day, optionally offset by days. Optionally uses the supplied IANA time zone for the day boundary.		{{ submittedDate | day_end: 0, "Europe/London" }} → end of that London date
day_offset(date, offset, time_zone)Adds days to date
Returns new date with specified number of days added. Optionally applies the offset in the supplied IANA time zone.		{{ "now" | day_offset: 7, "Europe/London" }} → date 7 days from now
day_start(date, offset, time_zone)Gets start of day (00:00:00)
Returns date at beginning of day, optionally offset by days. Optionally uses the supplied IANA time zone for the day boundary.		{{ submittedDate | day_start: 0, "Europe/London" }} → midnight at the start of that London date
excel_date(serial_date, offset, time_zone)Converts Excel serial date to Date
Converts Excel numeric date format to JavaScript Date. Optionally interprets the Excel date at midnight in the supplied IANA time zone.		{{ 44927 | excel_date: 0, "Europe/London" }} → converts Excel date number
format_currency(number, include_pence, round_even, locale, currency)Formats number as currency
Formats number as currency with locale and rounding options.		{{ 1234.56 | format_currency: true, false, "en-GB", "GBP" }}
format_date(date, format, time_zone)Formats date using specified format string
Uses date-fns formatting with custom format patterns. Optionally formats in the supplied IANA time zone.		{{ submittedDate | format_date: "dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm zzz", "Europe/London" }}
format_number(number, min_digits, max_digits)Formats number with specified decimal places
Formats number using en-GB locale with decimal control.		{{ 1234.5 | format_number: 2, 2 }} → 1,234.50
gfdate(gf_date_object, time_zone)Converts Govforms date object to JavaScript Date
Transforms {day, month, year} object to Date instance. Optionally interprets the date at midnight in the supplied IANA time zone.		{{ my_gf_date | gfdate: "Europe/London" }}
gfdate_to_date(gf_date_object, time_zone)Converts Govforms date to JavaScript Date
Same as gfdate filter - converts {day, month, year} to Date. Optionally interprets the date at midnight in the supplied IANA time zone.		{{ my_gf_date | gfdate_to_date: "Europe/London" }}
gfdate_to_string(gf_date_object, separator)Converts Govforms date to formatted string
Formats {day, month, year} as string with custom separator (default: "-").		{{ my_gf_date | gfdate_to_string: "/" }}
gftime_to_string(gf_time_object)Converts Govforms time object to string
Formats time object to HH:mm string format.		{{ my_gf_time | gftime_to_string }}
is_decimal(value)Checks if value is decimal number
Returns true if value is numeric and not an integer.		{{ 123.45 | is_decimal }} → true
is_number(value)Checks if value is numeric
Returns true if value can be parsed as a number.		{{ "123.45" | is_number }} → true
math(expression, ...variables)Evaluates mathematical expressions with variable substitution
Uses MathJS to evaluate expressions. Variables are mapped to a-z based on order.		{{ "((a-b) * 2 + 3) / c" | math: 5, myVar1, myVar2 }}
month_offset(date, offset, time_zone)Adds months to date
Returns new date with specified number of months added. Optionally applies the offset in the supplied IANA time zone.		{{ "now" | month_offset: 3, "Europe/London" }} → date 3 months from now
number(value)Converts value to number
Parses numeric value, returns empty string if not numeric.		{{ "123.45" | number }} → 123.45
parse_date(date_string, format, time_zone)Parses date string using specified format
Uses date-fns to parse date with custom format string. If an IANA time zone is supplied and the format does not include an offset/time zone token, the parsed local time is interpreted in that time zone.		{{ "2023-12-25 09:30" | parse_date: "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm", "Europe/London" }}
random(min, max)Generates random integer in range
Returns random integer between min and max (inclusive).		{{ 1 | random: 10 }} → random number 1-10
round_fixed(value, decimal_places)Rounds number to fixed decimal places
Returns string representation with exact number of decimal places.		{{ 123.456 | round_fixed: 2 }} → "123.46"
timestamp(date, offset, time_zone)Gets timestamp from date
Returns Unix timestamp (milliseconds). Use "now" for current time. Optionally interprets date-only values in the supplied IANA time zone.		{{ my_gf_date | timestamp: 0, "Europe/London" }}
to_iso_string(date, time_zone)Converts date to ISO 8601 string (UTC)
Returns a UTC ISO 8601 string (e.g. 2025-07-02T21:01:31.000Z). Accepts "now", a Govforms date object {day,month,year}, or a JavaScript Date. Optionally interprets date-only values in the supplied IANA time zone.		{{ my_gf_date | to_iso_string: "Europe/London" }} → 2025-07-01T23:00:00.000Z

Related guidance

  • Write Liquid templates
  • Use Markdown and HTML

articles.title: Links and navigation
articles.content:
Use these filters to encode URL values and create links that respect the current service and journey context. Prefer the accessible Govforms variants where available, and never expose review tokens or generated private URLs in logs or public content.

Standard Liquid filters

These filters are provided as standard by the Liquid language. They are available anywhere Govforms accepts a Liquid template.

FilterWhat it doesExample
cgi_escape()Escapes text for a CGI query string
Percent-encodes special characters and replaces spaces with plus signs.		{{ "hello world!" | cgi_escape }} → hello+world%21
slugify(mode, preserve_case)Converts text to a URL-friendly slug
Replaces unsupported characters with hyphens. The optional mode controls allowed characters.		{{ "Hello World" | slugify }} → hello-world
uri_escape()Escapes unsafe characters in a URI
Encodes unsafe characters while preserving URI separators such as slashes.		{{ "https://example.com/a path" | uri_escape }} → https://example.com/a%20path
url_decode()URL decodes string
Decodes URL-encoded characters.		{{ "hello%20world" | url_decode }} → hello world
url_encode()URL encodes string
Encodes special characters for URLs.		{{ "hello world" | url_encode }} → hello%20world

Govforms filters

These filters are added by Govforms for service-building and data-handling tasks.

FilterWhat it doesExample
completed_answers_link(link_text)Creates link to completed answers page
Generates HTML link to view submitted form answers.		{{ "View Answers" | completed_answers_link }}
external_service_link(link_text, url, classes, ...params)Creates external service link with parameters
Generates link to external URL with query parameters.		{{ "External Link" | external_service_link: "https://example.com", "btn", "param1", "value1" }}
external_service_link_accessible(link_text, visually_hidden_prefix, visually_hidden_suffix, url, classes, ...params)Creates accessible external service link
Like external_service_link but with screen reader text.		{{ "Link" | external_service_link_accessible: "Go to", "page", "https://example.com", "btn" }}
file_download_link(field_id, link_text)Creates file download link
Generates download link for uploaded file in specified field.		{{ "upload_field" | file_download_link: "Download File" }}
file_view_link(field_id, link_text)Creates file view link
Generates view link for uploaded file in specified field.		{{ "upload_field" | file_view_link: "View File" }}
get_query_param(url, param)Gets the value of query parameter within the given URL
Returns the query parameter value if present		{{ "https://test.com?a=1&b=2 | get_query_param: "b" }}
html_view_link(html_data_path_or_expression, link_text)Creates HTML view link
Generates a link to view HTML data returned by an action or expression.		{{ actions.fetchHtml.compressedHtml | html_view_link: "View HTML" }}
page_link(link_text, page_id, classes, ...params)Creates form page navigation link
Generates button to navigate to specific form page without validation.		{{ "Go to Page 2" | page_link: "page2", "btn" }}
page_link_accessible(link_text, visually_hidden_prefix, visually_hidden_suffix, page_id, classes, ...params)Creates accessible form page link
Like page_link but with screen reader text.		{{ "Continue" | page_link_accessible: "Go to", "next page", "page2", "btn" }}
page_submit_action(link_text, classes, ...params)Creates form submit action without navigation
Generates button to submit form data without changing pages.		{{ "Save" | page_submit_action: "btn-secondary" }}
page_submit_action_accessible(link_text, visually_hidden_prefix, visually_hidden_suffix, classes, ...params)Creates accessible form submit action
Like page_submit_action but with screen reader text.		{{ "Save" | page_submit_action_accessible: "Save", "progress", "btn" }}
page_submit_link(link_text, page_id, classes, ...params)Creates form page submit link with validation
Generates button to navigate to page with form validation.		{{ "Continue" | page_submit_link: "page2", "btn" }}
page_submit_link_accessible(link_text, visually_hidden_prefix, visually_hidden_suffix, page_id, classes, ...params)Creates accessible form page submit link
Like page_submit_link but with screen reader text.		{{ "Submit" | page_submit_link_accessible: "Submit", "form", "page2", "btn" }}
page_url(page_id, ...params)Gets full URL for form page
Returns complete URL for specified form page with parameters.		{{ "page2" | page_url: "param1", "value1" }}
pdf_download_link(action_id, link_text)Creates PDF download link
Generates HTML link to download PDF with specified action ID.		{{ "report1" | pdf_download_link: "Download PDF" }}
pdf_view_link(action_id, link_text)Creates PDF view link
Generates HTML link to view PDF in browser.		{{ "report1" | pdf_view_link: "View PDF" }}
print_link(link_text)Creates print page link
Generates HTML link that triggers browser print dialog.		{{ "Print Page" | print_link }}
reset_password_link(link_text)Creates link for signed-in user to change password
Generates HTML link to password change page. Only works for services using Cognito authentication.		{{ "Change your password" | reset_password_link }}
restart_link(link_text)Creates form restart link
Generates HTML link to restart the current form.		{{ "Start Over" | restart_link }}
review_token(action_id)Gets review access token for action
Returns access token for reviewing specific action or default token.		{{ "action1" | review_token }}
service_link(link_text, service_id, org, classes, ...params)Creates internal service link
Generates link to another service within the platform.		{{ "Other Service" | service_link: "service123", "myorg", "btn" }}
service_link_accessible(link_text, visually_hidden_prefix, visually_hidden_suffix, service_id, org, classes, ...params)Creates accessible internal service link
Like service_link but with screen reader text.		{{ "Link" | service_link_accessible: "Go to", "service", "service123", "myorg", "btn" }}
service_url(service_id, org, ...params)Gets URL for internal service
Returns just the URL for another service (no HTML link).		{{ "service123" | service_url: "myorg" }}

Related guidance

  • Write Liquid templates
  • Use Markdown and HTML

articles.title: Forms, fields and service
articles.content:
Use these filters when a template needs field or form output, component visibility information or the current repeating-row context. Pass inner field IDs—not an outer group ID—and test hidden, blank and repeated values.

Standard Liquid filters

These filters are provided as standard by the Liquid language. They are available anywhere Govforms accepts a Liquid template.

FilterWhat it doesExample
default(fallback)Provides fallback for empty values
Returns fallback if input is null, undefined, or empty string.		{{ empty_var | default: "N/A" }} → N/A
first()Gets first element of array
Returns first item in array or first character of string.		{{ "hello" | first }} → h
json()Converts value to JSON string
Serializes value as JSON.		{{ my_object | json }} → {"key":"value"}
last()Gets last element of array
Returns last item in array or last character of string.		{{ "hello" | last }} → o
map(property)Extracts property from array of objects
Creates array of property values from object array.		{{ users | map: "name" }} → array of name values
size()Returns size of array or string
Gets length/count of elements.		{{ "hello" | size }} → 5
where(property, expected)Selects matching array items
Returns objects whose property equals the expected value. If expected is omitted, the property must be truthy.		{{ users | where: "active", true | json }}

Govforms filters

These filters are added by Govforms for service-building and data-handling tasks.

FilterWhat it doesExample
field_to_text(field_value, field_id, field_defs, part_id)Converts field value to display text
Formats field value according to field type for display.		{{ my_field_value | field_to_text: "field1", form.fieldDefs }}
form_to_json(form)Converts form data to JSON object
Extracts all field values into clean JSON structure.		{{ form | form_to_json }}
form_to_text(form, newlines)Converts form data to formatted text
Creates human-readable text summary of form data.		{{ form | form_to_text: 2 }}
is_editing_table_group_iteration(field_in_group_id)Checks if currently editing table group row
Pass the ID of a field inside the group. The group itself is not addressed by ID.		{{ "line_item_name" | is_editing_table_group_iteration }}
is_hidden(field_id)Checks if field is hidden by conditional logic
Returns true if field is currently hidden by show/hide rules.		{{ "conditional_field" | is_hidden }}
is_visible(field_id)Checks if field is visible
Returns true if field is currently visible (opposite of is_hidden).		{{ "conditional_field" | is_visible }}
not(boolean)Logical NOT operation
Returns opposite boolean value.		{{ true | not }} → false
show_hidden_component(change_text, reset_text, visually_hidden_prefix, visually_hidden_suffix, field_id, classes, iteration, dont_save)Creates toggle for hidden form components
Generates button to show/hide optional form fields.		{{ "Add details" | show_hidden_component: "Remove details", "", "", "optional_field", "btn-link" }}

articles.title: What is Govforms?
articles.content: Govforms is a no-code digital service builder that helps teams create, deploy, and manage GDS-compliant online forms and workflows without needing developers.

articles.title: Who is Govforms for?
articles.content: Govforms is designed for public sector, education, and enterprise teams who need to deliver digital services quickly, securely, and accessibly.

articles.title: Do I need technical skills to use Govforms?
articles.content: No. Govforms includes drag-and-drop tools, templates, and a visual logic editor so you can build services without any coding experience.

articles.title: How long does it take to go live?
articles.content: Most services go live in days or weeks. You can build, test, and deploy through QA and Production environments with just a few clicks.

articles.title: Can I host my service on a custom domain?
articles.content: Yes. Govforms supports custom domain configurations, allowing services to run under your departmental or organizational domain while maintaining full SSL security.

articles.title: Does Govforms support file uploads?
articles.content: Yes. The platform includes secure, configurable file upload components for documents, media, or images, with virus scanning, validation, and size restrictions to meet compliance needs.

articles.title: Can I include video or media content?
articles.content: Yes. You can embed video explainers, guidance clips, or media content within your forms or service journeys to improve user understanding and engagement.

articles.title: Does Govforms include analytics or reporting tools?
articles.content: A built-in real-time dashboard provides insight into submissions, completion rates, device usage, and user drop-offs, helping teams refine and optimize services.

articles.title: How is data stored and protected?
articles.content: All data is UK-hosted on ISO 27001-certified infrastructure. Every form submission is encrypted in transit and at rest, with detailed audit trails and access logs.

articles.title: Can Govforms integrate with existing systems like SharePoint or Dataverse?
articles.content: Yes. Govforms supports direct integrations with Microsoft SharePoint, Dataverse, APIs, and authentication systems (SSO/OAuth) to streamline data flow between services.

articles.title: Is Govforms suitable for Whitehall departments or regulated sectors?
articles.content: Absolutely. Govforms is designed for compliance with government and regulatory data handling requirements, making it suitable for Whitehall departments, research councils, and public sector agencies.

articles.title: Does Govforms meet government data standards?
articles.content: Yes. The platform aligns with UK Government Digital Service (GDS) and GDPR data handling standards.

articles.title: How is security managed?
articles.content: Govforms uses TLS 1.2+ encryption, access control, environment isolation, and regular penetration testing.

articles.title: What types of services can be built with Govforms?
articles.content: From grant applications and consultation forms to license requests, registrations, and reporting tools. Govforms powers a wide range of digital services for government and public sector teams.

articles.title: Can I use Govforms for internal services?
articles.content: Yes. Many teams use Govforms for internal workflows, approvals, and reporting systems, not just public-facing forms.

articles.title: How does Govforms extend to private sector use cases?
articles.content: Private sector clients use Govforms for secure data collection, compliance processes, and public engagement. It’s ideal for organizations needing GDS-level accessibility and structure.

articles.title: What authentication methods does Govforms support?
articles.content:
Govforms supports seven authentication methods to match your service requirements.

•  Anonymous access for public-facing forms with no sign-in.
•  GOV.UK Notify magic link for passwordless email-based sign-in.
• OIDC/OAuth 2.0 for connecting to your existing identity provider such as Azure AD or any compliant provider.
•  AWS Cognito with hosted user pools and MFA.
• Configurable session timeouts with user warnings.
• Save-and-return in single-draft, multi-journey, or one-and-done modes.
•  Group-based sharing so users in the same group can view each other’s submissions.

Each method can be configured per service, and you can combine authentication with role-based read-only access for staff review scenarios.

articles.title: Can Govforms integrate with non-Microsoft systems?
articles.content:
Yes. Alongside deep Microsoft integration, Govforms includes a full REST API client connecting to any system with an HTTP endpoint, with custom headers, authentication including client certificates, and mock responses for testing.

GOV.UK Notify, AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage are all supported natively. All integrations are configurable per environment.

articles.title: What API integration capabilities are available?
articles.content:
The REST API action provides a full HTTP client. You can configure the HTTP method, URL, headers, and authentication including OAuth tokens, API keys, and mutual TLS with client certificates.

Request bodies use Liquid templates for full payload control and conditional logic. Response fields map back into the service. Mock responses available for testing, conditional action firing, and email alerts on production failures.

articles.title: How does environment promotion work?
articles.content:
Every service has three environments:
1. Prototype (instant updates, shareable preview links)
2. QA (full integration testing and UAT against test systems)
3. Production (live, with custom departmental domains and full SSL).

Promote between environments in a few clicks. Every promotion is tracked, and you can revert to any previous version at any stage.
